_comment: The Forum's rooms, in the order the Forum lists them, and the team's threads in each. The one list: ops/discourse/rooms.rb makes the rooms and threads on Discourse (run by .github/workflows/forum-theme.yml before every theme release), core/forum.py limits the public feed to these rooms, and core/test_forum_rooms.py fails if the theme (components/graviquest/forum-home.gjs) lists different rooms. Slugs and thread keys are permanent; names, descriptions, titles and bodies may change. These are the team's threads; members may start their own, which a moderator reads first. A thread marked existing was posted earlier (by bootstrap.rb); rooms.rb only keeps it in its room and its title in step, and never rewrites its text.

rooms.name: About the Forum
rooms.description: What this place is for, how a thread works, and the few rules we keep.

threads.title: Welcome to the GraviQuest Forum
threads.body:
This is where the GraviQuest community talks things through.

**How it works**

- Open a room and read any thread. No account is needed to read.
- Each thread opens with a post from the team. Sign in with your GraviQuest account to reply to it, or to any reply under it, and to like posts.

**The rules we keep**

1. Take a position, then say why.
2. Cite it, or say you cannot.
3. A moderator reads member posts before they appear.

Questions about the Forum itself are welcome below.

threads.title: What GraviQuest is
threads.body:
GraviQuest is a community drawn together by the weighty questions in science and AI, with a forum to talk them through.

Each Topic takes one question and explores it through videos, essays and discussion. Topic 01 starts with an AI assistant that hands back a correct number, and asks what that actually proved.

[See the Topics](https://graviquest.com/topics.html) · [How the community works](https://graviquest.com/community)

Questions about GraviQuest itself are welcome below.

rooms.name: Topic 01 · AI in Research
rooms.description: Watch, read, then talk it through: one thread for the videos, one for the essays, one for the discussion.

threads.title: Videos: The Answer That Looked Right
threads.body:
Our first video: Professor Hulse, his student Taylor, and an AI assistant that hands back a correct number.

Where would you have stopped it and asked for the source? Say which moment, and what you would have checked.

[Watch it on the Topic page](https://graviquest.com/topic-answer-that-looked-right.html)

threads.title: Essays: claim by claim
threads.body:
Respond to the Topic 01 essays here.

Quote the claim you are answering, say whether its source holds, and link a better one if you have it.

[Read them on the Topic page](https://graviquest.com/topic-answer-that-looked-right.html)
